story.title: Two fatalities in school bus crash in eastern France
story.summary: A school bus carrying 43 passengers crashed into a tree in eastern France, resulting in the deaths of a seven-year-old girl and an 18-year-old man. Several others were reported injured in the incident, according to local authorities.

explore_lenses.label: What kind of bus service was involved?
explore_lenses.title: A regional route, not a dedicated school bus
explore_lenses.summary: The crash involved an intercity bus on the Lyon–Bourg-en-Bresse route that also carried students. That distinction matters because the victims and passengers included both school-bound minors and other regular-route travelers.

claims.text: Prosecutors said the bus had 43 passengers, including 15 minors travelling to school, while it was operating between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse.
Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot described it as a bus run by the regional authority and carrying about 15 students alongside other passengers.
Local reporting identified the operator as Keolis and described the vehicle as serving an interurban route rather than being exclusively a school service.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about the cause?
explore_lenses.title: The cause remains undetermined
explore_lenses.summary: Accounts establish that the bus crossed from its lane and struck trees, but authorities had not publicly identified a cause by November 6. Early screening did not indicate alcohol or drugs, and the driver had not yet been interviewed because he was hospitalized.

claims.text: A 17-year-old passenger said the bus had been in its right-hand lane before making a sharp steering movement, crossing into the left-hand lane and going into a ditch; this is eyewitness evidence, not an official finding on cause.
Ain prefect Louis-Xavier Thirode said preliminary blood tests on the driver found no traces of alcohol or drugs.
Lent Mayor Yves Cristin said the road was slightly wet but not foggy and that officials did not understand why the bus left the road; he described the road as well maintained.
The driver was hospitalized and had not yet been heard by investigators, according to reporting citing the prosecutor's office.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the emergency response?
explore_lenses.title: A road-homicide inquiry and victim support
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate response combined a large rescue operation with a criminal investigation. The inquiry is intended to determine responsibility, while survivors and relatives were directed to local psychological and victim-support services.

claims.text: The Bourg-en-Bresse prosecutor opened an investigation for road homicide; reporting says it was assigned to the Lyon gendarmerie's investigative section.
Authorities deployed 102 firefighters, four aircraft and eight ground emergency medical teams, while Lent opened its community hall for victims.
The Ain victim-support association Avema was asked to provide a psychological support unit for shocked passengers and the parents of injured or deceased minors.

story_report.summary: A bus carrying 43 passengers crashed into a tree in eastern France, killing a seven-year-old girl and an 18-year-old man. Several other people were injured, according to local authorities. Prosecutors said 15 of those aboard were minors travelling to school on a service operating between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse.

sections.heading: Regional bus service carried students
sections.body: Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said the vehicle was run by the regional authority and carried about 15 students as well as other passengers. Local reporting identified the operator as Keolis and described the route as an interurban service, rather than one exclusively for schoolchildren.

sections.heading: Investigators examine cause of crash
sections.body: A 17-year-old passenger said the bus had been travelling in its right-hand lane before making a sharp movement, crossing into the left lane and entering a ditch; the account is eyewitness testimony rather than an official finding. The driver was hospitalized and had not yet been interviewed, while preliminary blood tests found no traces of alcohol or drugs. The Bourg-en-Bresse prosecutor opened a road-homicide investigation assigned to the Lyon gendarmerie's investigative section.

sections.heading: Emergency response supports passengers and families
sections.body: Authorities deployed 102 firefighters, four aircraft and eight ground emergency medical teams, and Lent opened its community hall for victims. The Ain victim-support association Avema was asked to provide psychological support for shocked passengers and for parents of injured or deceased minors.

unresolved.text: The cause of the crash had not been publicly established. Officials had not determined whether a medical event, vehicle condition, speed, road conditions or another factor was involved, and no timetable had been announced for driver questioning, technical examinations or possible proceedings.
Public reporting did not establish the full passenger manifest or why particular passengers were travelling on the service.

related_stories.title: Bomb Threats Target Irish Media and European Newsrooms
related_stories.summary: A series of bomb threats have led to the evacuation of newsrooms across Ireland and Bulgaria. The threats were reportedly made by an individual identifying as 'Mikhail Andropov'. This incident comes ahead of a high-level EU meeting scheduled to take place in Dublin soon.

related_stories.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie Sentenced to 200 Years for Mass Murders
related_stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie, the leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult. He was convicted for inciting his followers to starve themselves to death as part of a belief that they would meet Jesus. The court's decision follows a trial that included 28 co-defendants, and Mackenzie plans to appeal.

related_stories.title: California Governor Commutes All Death Sentences to Life Without Parole
related_stories.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced that he will commute the sentences of all 548 death row inmates in the state to life in prison without the possibility of parole. He stated that capital punishment is morally wrong, and the state Supreme Court will have the final authority on these cases.

related_stories.title: Thomas Markle Sr. Arrested in Florida on Child Abuse Material Charges
related_stories.summary: Thomas Markle Sr., the estranged father of Meghan Markle, was arrested by federal agents in Florida on charges related to the possession of child sexual abuse material. The arrest follows an investigation that began after his son reportedly discovered boxes containing numerous images at his father's former home in the Philippines. Meghan Markle expressed that she is 'deeply distressed' by the charges against her father.
